harder.updated_question: substrat buatan dalam trasplantasi karang berikan penjelasan berserta sumbernya
harder.verification_criterion: The answer includes at least one credible academic or scientific source (journal article, research paper, or authoritative publication) cited to support the explanation of artificial substrates in coral transplantation.

attempts.answer:
Pendahuluan: Apa itu substrat buatan dalam transplantasi karang
- Substrat buatan adalah struktur keras yang dipasang di dasar laut untuk memberikan permukaan yang stabil dan kompleks bagi fragmen karang diberi makan, reproduksi, dan pertumbuhan, terutama di tempat dimana substrat alami (karang tua, kerikil karang) rusak, longsor, atau tidak tersedia bagi larva dan potongan karang dewasa. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Coral reefs often degrade into rubble after storms; this rubble shifts with currents, forming ‘killing fields’ for juvenile corals that hinder recovery, so artificial substrates are used for coral transplantation and recruitment</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Coral transplantation is commonly done by placing fragments on tables or cages and then transferring them to rehabilitation sites; combining artificial reefs with transplantation is recommended to optimize rehabilitation</cite>.

- Secara historis dan praktis, substrat buatan juga dirancang sebagai “habitat sementara” agar karang cepat menempel dan tumbuh, kemudian beralih menjadi substrat alami bagi komunitas invertebrata dan ikan lainnya. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Various materials have been used for artificial reefs worldwide, including ceramic, concrete, wood, bamboo, plastic and metal; each has drawbacks, and ceramic materials can be economical, environmentally safe and suitable for hostile marine environments</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-2">Ceramic reefs are non-toxic, pH-neutral, mechanically strong and durable, with high water absorption that provides microhabitats for microbes and good shelter for small fish</cite>.

Mengapa substrat buatan dibutuhkan dalam transplantasi karang
- Kerusakan massal (tsunami, badai) menghasilkan kerikil yang bergerak dan mekanisnya merendahkan kelangsungan hidup larva dan potongan karang. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Rubble created by tsunamis and storms moves with currents, acting as lethal ‘killing fields’ for coral juveniles and impeding recovery</cite>. 
- Transplantasi memerlukan permukaan keras berdaya dukung biologis (porositas, ketidaklicin, kompleksitas tekstur) dan daya tahan struktural bagi potongan karang. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Transplantation generally involves transferring fragments to rehabilitation areas, but transplanting can impose stress and donor losses, making integration with artificial substrates important</cite>.
- Dengan substrat buatan, teknisi dapat mengontrol morfologi permukaan, posisi pemasangan, dan menjaga ketersediaan ruang bagi penempelan dan pertumbuhan. <cite id="d94f8397-4">Artificial Patch Reefs (APR) provide multilevel substrates integrating coral transplantation and artificial reefs to create hard substrate in shallow turbid waters</cite>.

Kategori bahan substrat buatan dan sifat-sifatnya
1) Bahan beton dan struktur beton terkombinasi (dalam bentuk blok, tetrapod, panel, atau unit terasering)
- Beton/Portland cement sering dipakai karena daya dukung struktural dan fleksibilitas bentuk, tetapi cenderung mahal dan perlu perencanaan daya tahan terhadap erosi dan dinamika arus. <cite id="96dceb75-4">Assembled concrete reefs are designed to resist monsoon sea conditions; prior art includes single tetrapod artificial coral concretes, spatial-shaped and semicircular forms, combinable blocks, polyethylene-pipe and coconut-shell structures</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Concrete blocks are durable and configurable but limited by cost</cite>.
- Komposisi beton (pasir basalt/limestone/recycled aggregate) tidak selalu memengaruhi penyerapan larva secara signifikan, tetapi kondisi situs dan topografi sangat penting. <cite id="70533d8a-1">Concrete plates with basalt, limestone, and recycled aggregate showed no significant difference in mean coral recruits across compositions, while environments (lab, deep water, shallow field) caused large differences (86±11, 135±15, 4±1 recruits), emphasizing the role of site conditions</cite>.
- Daya dukung biologis meningkat ketika permukaan berpori, tidak licin, dan berstruktur kompleks, sesuai dengan pola alami karang. <cite id="70533d8a-2">Ceramic surfaces are porous, non-slippery without glaze, provide microhabitats, and support microbial productivity and fish sheltering</cite>.

2) Keramik/terak liat (earthenware, tanah liat firi/stoneware tanpa gliser)
- Keramik unglazed sering dipakai sebagai substrat penempelan dan panel eksperimen; porositas dan tekstur meningkatkan penempelan. <cite id="96dceb75-1">Unglazed ceramic settlement tiles are commonly used in coral recruitment studies; a stoneware clay fired up to 1150°C without glaze can serve as an artificial reef with non-slippery surfaces that support coral settlement due to porosity</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Larva Dendronephthya labyrinthiformis only settled on lime-mortar-based substrates compared to acrylic/PDMS, indicating base material choice strongly influences settlement</cite>.
- Data mekanik menunjukkan keramik kuat secara tekan dan tahan erosi, tetapi kurang lentur dan rentan erosi oleh partikel besar; tetap demikian, ia aman secara kimia dan mendukung kolonisasi. <cite id="70533d8a-2">Ceramic reefs are non-toxic, pH-neutral, mechanically strong, but have lower flexural strength (~4.5 MPa vs coral ~13.8 MPa) and higher erosion under ≥1.2 mm sand particle erosion</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-3">A ceramic wall of 24 mm thickness can withstand ~1031 N static load, suggesting good static stability</cite>.

3) Mortar kapur dan bahan kalsium karbonat alami/buatan
- Mortar kapur (Ca(OH)2/air) yang berkarbonasi menjadi aragonit/kalsit menawarkan sinyal penempelan kuat bagi larva; komposisi dan laju karbonasi kritis untuk keselamatan dan fisiologi karang. <cite id="96dceb75-3">D. labyrinthiformis larvae only settled on lime mortar substrates; carbonate phase and additive chemistry (e.g., aragonite, bioactive glass) modulate settlement cues</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-2">Additives such as quartz sand, glass fibers, bioactive glass, and carbonate minerals altered surface characteristics; carbonate conversion to CaCO3 proceeded >98% under high CO2, while unreacted Ca(OH)2 can produce high pH that may be harmful to corals</cite>.
- Teknologi ini memungkinkan sequester CO2 secara fungsional sekaligus meningkatkan biokompatibilitas permukaan. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Lime mortar carbonation sequesters CO2 but is slow; accelerating carbonation in high CO2 environments (>99% conversion by PXRD) mitigates harmful unreacted Ca(OH)2</cite>.

4) RUBBLE yang diproses/diikat (kerangka dari kerikil karang alami)
- Kerikil karang organik yang dipertahankan tetapi diorganisir dengan jaring (nylon/PET) menjadi substrat murah, lokal, dan topografis kompleks; cocok untuk pengganti parsial beton di daerah patah patah. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Modified coral rubble bound by nylon or polyethylene nets formed compact, stable, complex-surface substrates that supported Acropora formosa growth; this low-cost approach uses locally available nets and can replace concrete bases, though broader replication is needed</cite>.
- Desain “furnace” dan panel berlubang menawarkan kompartemen transplantasi sederhana dan efisien di medan pelayaran. <cite id="d94f8397-0">Transplantation modules mixed cement-sand and formed furnace-like structures with six holes per module for Acropora fragments; the design improved efficiency under Anambas water conditions</cite>.

5) Bahan polimer dan 3D-print (akrylik, PDMS, dan cetakan lapisan)
- Bahan sintetis seperti PMMA/akrylik dan PDMS kurang diminati larva dibanding bahan kalsium karbonat; akrylik/PDMS tidak menawarkan sinyal penempelan kuat bagi larva laut. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Coral larvae only settled on lime mortar substrates; acrylic and PDMS substrates were not chosen by larvae</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-2">Surface roughness, fiber content, and mineral additives modulate settlement; carbonate-based composites outperformed noncarbonate polymer controls</cite>.
- Namun, bahan polimer/metal/plastic sering dipakai untuk panel eksperimen, struktur sementara, dan bentuk 3D terenkapsulasi yang menyerap air dan memberi rongga mikro bagi penempelan yang berkembang. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Polyvinyl chloride pipes and other plastics are used but ceramics often better support fish colonization than concrete and PVC</cite>.

Prinsip desain substrat buatan yang memengaruhi penempelan dan pertumbuhan
- Kompleksitas topografi: karang menempel dan tumbuh lebih baik di permukaan berpori, kasar, dan berirama (makro/mikrotopografi), mirip dengan struktur karang alami. <cite id="70533d8a-1">High coral cover occurred on adjacent natural reefs with spur-and-groove macro- and microtopographic complexity; sparse cover on concrete armor units and bare sand/rubble nearby</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-4">APR multilevel substrates add vertical complexity to create hard substrate for Acropora growth in shallow turbid waters</cite>.
- Sifat permukaan: non-slippery/unglazed, tekstur kasar, dan adhesi biokimia (kalsium karbonat, aragonit, bioactive glass) meningkatkan afinitas larva. <cite id="96dceb75-1">Unglazed ceramic surfaces avoid slippery glaze layers, allowing coral juveniles to live and thrive due to porous surfaces</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-2">Lime mortar composites with quartz sand, glass fibers, and bioactive glass increased settlement enhancing cues, with >98% carbonate conversion after high CO2 carbonation</cite>.
- Stabilitas hidrodinamis: struktur harus tahan guncang arus dan gelombang, sekaligus memberi perlindungan lokal bagi potongan karang. <cite id="96dceb75-4">Assembled concrete reefs are designed to withstand monsoon sea conditions</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Nets-stabilized modified coral rubble provided stability and complexity for transplantation at low cost</cite>.
- Orientasi dan pencahayaan: orientasi terhadap arah gelombang dan kedalaman memengaruhi penempelan dan kelangsungan hidup. <cite id="70533d8a-1">Design should emulate spur-and-groove complexity and orientation with wave direction and water depth</cite>.

Metode pemasangan dan teknik transplantasi pada substrat buatan
- Panel/kerangka dipasang di dasar laut dan ditusuk lubang untuk menempatkan potongan karang; potongan diikat/epoksi/tekuk ke permukaan berpori. <cite id="d94f8397-0">Each furnace-shaped module had six holes for transplanting Acropora fragments, integrating media and fish shelter</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Transplantation methods can stress donor colonies and reduce growth/fecundity; integrating with artificial reefs mitigates these impacts</cite>.
- Untuk karang Acropora (tumbuh cepat dan tahan fragmentasi), substrat berlapis/multilevel cocok di perairan turbid dan dangkal; efektivitas dipengaruhi metode pemasangan dan daya lekat antara potongan dan substrat. <cite id="d94f8397-4">APR with Acropora on multilevel substrates aims to enhance growth and survival in shallow turbid waters; fixing methods and species selection are under study</cite>.
- Bahan alternatif “kerikil alami dikemas” cocok di daerah patah-patah bencana, jika dikontrol secara struktural agar tidak berpindah. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Modified coral rubble with nets formed a compact, cost-effective, locally available substrate that supported Acropora growth but needs replication across sites</cite>.

Pertimbangan ekologis dan risiko bahan
- Kimia dan toksisitas: bahan harus netral pH, tidak melepaskan racun, dan aman bagi larva/i; porositas memungkinkan pertukaran air dan nutrisi. <cite id="70533d8a-0">Ceramic artificial reefs were nontoxic, pH-neutral, mechanically strong, sustainable, and safe for small fish</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Unreacted Ca(OH)2 in incompletely carbonated lime mortar can produce high pH that is harmful to corals, necessitating accelerated carbonation</cite>.
- Dekomposisi mekanis dan usia: beton tahan tetapi rentan erosi dan beban dinamis; keramik kuat tekan tetapi lemah lentur; lime mortar memerlukan karbonasi sempurna dan perlindungan kimia untuk daya tahan jangka panjang. <cite id="70533d8a-2">Ceramic flexural strength is lower than coral and erosion by ≥1.2 mm sand particles is significant, indicating durability under strong dynamic loads needs improvement</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Complete conversion to CaCO3 (>99%) by high CO2 and proper curing is needed to avoid harmful alkalinity</cite>.
- Kolonisasi biota: substrat buatan cepat dihuni alga, plankton, dan invertebrata kecil; ini diinginkan untuk mempercepat ekosistem, tetapi perlu diawasi agar tidak merusak karang pindah atau menumbuhkan alga dominan yang menghambat. <cite id="70533d8a-2">Ceramic reefs support continuous propagation of plankton and other benthic organisms and provide good shelter for small fish</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Placing any material in marine environments risks pollution and harmful effects; ceramic is often preferred due to better fish colonization and safety</cite>.
- Bahan organik (kayu/bambu) rentan terputus dan mengendap, merusak dasar; plastik metal berisiko polusi, meski biaya rendah. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Bamboo and wood are easily scattered by currents, losing fish-aggregating integrity and degrading the seabed; plastics pose pollution risks; ceramics often better balance ecological and structural needs</cite>.

Contoh penerapan di Indonesia dan kasus nyata
- Seribu (DKI Jakarta): substrat buatan dari kerikil karang alami yang diikat jaring (nylon/PET) bekerja sebagai media transplantasi murah lokal, mendukung pertumbuhan Acropora formosa; tetap perlu uji di lokasi lain dan waktu panjang. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Modified coral rubble with nylon/polyethylene nets formed stable, complex-surface substrates that supported Acropora growth; approach is low-cost and locally sourced but needs replication</cite>.
- Anambas (Kepulauan Riau): modul kombinasi beton-sand dengan bentuk “furnace” yang efisien, mengintegrasikan media transplantasi dan sarang ikan. <cite id="d94f8397-0">Transplantation modules mixed cement-sand into furnace-shaped units with six holes, designed for local hydrodynamic conditions</cite>.
- Kombinasi APR + transplantasi Acropora di perairan dangkal: menambah ruang hidup karang dan struktur kehidupan bagi komunitas lain; efektivitas dipengaruhi oleh metode pemasangan dan spesies karang. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Combining artificial reefs and coral transplantation is recommended to optimize rehabilitation</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-4">APR multilevel substrates aim to facilitate growth and survival of Acropora fragments in shallow turbid waters; fixing methods influence outcomes</cite>.

Pilihan bahan dan rekomendasi praktis berdasarkan konteks
- Di perairan berarus tinggi/monsoon: prioritaskan struktur beton/keramik yang tahan beban dinamis; gunakan desain berlapis dan arah gelombang. <cite id="96dceb75-4">Assembled concrete reefs are designed to resist monsoon conditions</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-1">Emulating spur-and-groove complexity and aligning with wave direction and depth improve coral development</cite>.
- Di daerah pasca-bencana karang (kerikil berlebih): prioritaskan substrat berbasis kerikil alami yang diproses (dengan jaring/bantalan) untuk biaya rendah dan adaptasi lokal; tambahkan batu bata/lapisan kalsium karbonat untuk afinitas penempelan. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Modified coral rubble with nets provided stable, complex-surface, low-cost substrates supporting Acropora</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-2">Calcium phosphate and lime mortar composite additives increased settlement cues in controlled experiments</cite>.
- Untuk laboratorium/program penempelan awal: pilih keramik unglazed berpori dan mortar kapur yang benar-benar berkarbonasi untuk memaksimalkan afinitas larva; pastikan pH netral dan tidak beracun. <cite id="96dceb75-1">Unglazed, porous ceramic tiles support coral settlement</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Lime mortar substrates were settled-on exclusively by Dendronephthya larvae, with carbonate conversion and additive chemistry modulating settlement</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Accelerated carbonation in high CO2 mitigates harmful unreacted Ca(OH)2</cite>.
- Hindari bahan organik tumbuh (kayu/bambu) dan plastik murni di area kritis, kecuali sebagai struktur sementara yang dirancang cepat kolonisasi biologis; gunakan epoxy/ikatan tahan air dan uji kelayakan hidrolik sebelum pemasangan massal. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Organic materials like bamboo/wood are easily dispersed; plastics can pollute; ceramics often provide better ecological performance</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Transplantation can stress donor colonies; careful integration with artificial substrates and fixing methods is essential</cite>.

Kesimpulan
- Substrat buatan adalah tulang punggung teknologi transplantasi karang modern, yang memperbaiki ketersediaan permukaan, struktur, dan stabilitas hidrodinamis di tempat substrat alami rusak atau tidak cukup. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Artificial substrates are used both for coral transplantation and recruitment to overcome lethal juvenile habitats formed by rubble</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Combining artificial reefs with transplantation is recommended to optimize rehabilitation</cite>.
- Pemilihan bahan dan desain substrat perlu seimbang antara mekanik (daya dukung dan daya tahan), biokimia (kimia permukaan dan fasa karbonat), dan ekologi (toksisitas, kolonisasi, serta proses alami). <cite id="96dceb75-3">Material base, carbonate phase, and additive chemistry strongly influence larval settlement</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-0">Ceramic artificial reefs are nontoxic and pH-neutral while providing mechanical strength and habitat</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-1">Topographic complexity and site conditions are critical to coral recruitment and community development</cite>.
- Praktik terbaik: gunakan bahan aman dan tahan (keramik, beton, mortar kapur yang terkarbonasi), tambahkan tekstur/porositas dan kompleksitas multi-skala, pasang secara hidrodinamis stabil, dan uji skala kecil sebelum implementasi luas. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Low-cost net-stabilized rubble substrates supported Acropora growth and are promising but need broader replication</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-4">Assembled concrete reefs demonstrate modular assembly for resisting adverse conditions</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-0">Field-tested furnace-shaped modules integrate transplantation media and fish shelter</cite>.

Sumber rujukan utama
- Field-tested local innovations and rationale: Growth Rate of Acropora formosa Fragments that Transplanted on Artificial Substrate Made from Coral Rubble. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Corals killed by tsunamis/storms form ‘killing fields’ of rubble; modified coral rubble with nets served as low-cost, stable, complex-surface substrates supporting Acropora transplantation</cite>.
- Material science and settlement cues: Composite Substrates Reveal Inorganic Material Cues for Coral Larval Settlement. <cite id="96dceb75-2">Surface roughness, porosity, and additives modulated settlement; lime mortar composites outperformed controls; carbonate phase and conversion to CaCO3 were critical</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Larvae only settled on lime mortar; carbonate conversion and additives like aragonite and bioactive glass enhanced cues; unreacted Ca(OH)2 needs mitigation</cite>.
- Ecological engineering and design principles: Ecoengineering considerations for coral reefs. <cite id="70533d8a-1">No significant differences in recruits among concrete compositions across basalt/limestone/recycled aggregate, but strong differences across environments; spur-and-groove complexity and orientation matter</cite>.
- Ceramic artificial reefs: Development and impacts. <cite id="70533d8a-0">Ceramic artificial reefs nontoxic, pH-neutral, mechanically strong, sustainable</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-2">Mechanical strengths and erosion resistance; good shelter for small fish; microbial propagation on porous surfaces</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-3">Manufacturing and comparative density to coral rubbles</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Ceramic often better colonized and safer than concrete/PVC; drawbacks and considerations</cite>.
- Indonesian case studies and integration with APR: Enhancing reef fish diversity using artificial reef-building (Nyamuk Island). <cite id="d94f8397-0">Cement-sand modules in furnace-like APR integrating transplant media and fish shelter</cite>. Transplantasi karang di APR multilevel. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Transplantation can stress donors and reduce growth/fecundity; integrating APR improves outcomes</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-4">APR multilevel substrates for Acropora with study of fixing methods</cite>.
- Modular concrete and assembled reefs: Assembled concrete reefs as a stand for coral transplantation. <cite id="96dceb75-4">Modular concrete reefs designed for monsoon resistance and efficient assembly</cite>.

Pertanyaan praktis tambahan yang sering muncul
- Apakah karang mungkin menempel pada bahan polimer/akrylik? Larva cenderung tidak memilih akrylik/PDMS dibanding bahan kalsium karbonat, meski permukaan berpori dan kasar bisa meningkatkan daya tempel. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Larvae only settled on lime mortar substrates compared to acrylic/PDMS</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-2">Surface roughness and mineralogy of carbonate composites enhance settlement versus noncarbonate polymer controls</cite>.
- Bagaimana memastikan substrat tidak beracun? Uji kimia pH dan toksisitas sebelum pemasangan; hindari bahan yang melepaskan ion beracun; pastikan mortar kapur benar-benar berkarbonasi. <cite id="70533d8a-0">Ceramic reefs were nontoxic and pH-neutral in long-term aquaria tests</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Unreacted Ca(OH)2 can be harmful; accelerate carbonation to >99% conversion</cite>.
- Apakah kerikil alami dari lokasi patah-patah bisa dipakai tanpa beton? Bisa, jika diproses struktural (ikat jaring, bentuk panel) agar stabil dan tetap kompleks permukaan; cocok untuk restorasi berbasis masyarakat. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Nets-encased modified coral rubble replaced concrete as a low-cost, locally available substrate supporting Acropora growth</cite>.

Catatan: Hasil spesifik bervariasi berdasarkan kondisi situs (arus, salinitas, pencahayaan) dan spesies karang; lakukan uji kecil (pilot) dan monitore secara rutin untuk menyesuaikan desain substrat dan teknik pemasangan. <cite id="70533d8a-1">Environmental site conditions (lab, deep water, shallow field) produced large differences in coral recruitment on concrete plates</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Transplantation success and fish-aggregation also depend on integration with artificial reef structures and fixing methods</cite>.

Snippet: Coral Larvae Exhibit a Preference for Lime Mortar Substrates. In search of a more effective larval settlement substrate, we first conducted a preliminary trial of substrates with different topographies, additives, and base materials ( Figure 1a). Strikingly, regardless of the additive composition or surface topography, D. labyrinthiformis larvae only settled on substrates made with lime mortar as the base material ( Figure 1a). Title: Development of Artificial Reefs Using Environmentally Safe Ceramic Material
Snippet: To develop artificial reefs, that are environmentally friendly and inexpensive, prototype artificial reefs made of ceramic material have been studied. The properties of the reefs (chemical constituents, surface texture, water absorbability, mechanical strength, erosion rate, and sustainability) were examined. The reefs were compared with natural coral rubbles. The effects of the reefs on nutrient availability, toxic chemical diffusion, and the propagation of plankton (bacteria, diatom) and other benthic organisms were examined, for which the reefs were set in aquaria for a long time. It was shown that the reefs were nontoxic, pH-neutral, mechanically strong, and sustainable in a hostile shallow sea environment. This study suggests that artificial reefs made from the ceramic material are not hazardous to small fish.
</snippet>

Title: ECOLOGICAL ENGINEERING CONSIDERATIONS FOR CORAL REEFS IN THE DESIGN OF MULTIFUNCTIONAL COASTAL STRUCTURES
Snippet: A multifunctional structure is being designed for the Kahului Harbor, Maui, Hawai‘i, to mitigate operational problems caused by wave energy while also providing coral reef habitat. There is limited information on how the design of a coastal structure can be manipulated to enhance the ecology of targeted coral communities. To inform the ecological engineering of an artificial coral reef, the relationship between substrate characteristics and coral colonization was investigated through coral recruitment experiments and study of field conditions. Three concrete compositions that differed by the use of basalt, limestone, or recycled aggregates were tested in field and laboratory experiments to determine the impact of each substrate on the recruitment of juvenile hermatypic corals. The concrete test plates were deployed in three environments for a period of about one year, after which the coral recruits on each plate were identified and counted. No significant difference was found in the average number of coral recruits on the concrete mixed with basalt, limestone and recycled aggregate (60 ± 9, 83 ± 17 and 77 ± 14, respectively). Significant differences in coral recruitment were found due to the laboratory tanks, deep water, and shallow water field tests environments (86 ± 11, 135 ± 15 and 4 ± 1, respectively). These results highlight the importance of environmental site conditions for the development of coral reef habitat. A field study was conducted in the vicinity of purposed artificial reef site to relate the topographic features of the surrounding environment to the levels of live coral coverage. The benthic zone was surveyed using a drop camera system and by divers who recorded in-situ observations. Of the area surveyed, the highest density of coral coverage (>90% cover on 60% of the area) was found on an adjacent natural reef area that was characterized by spur and groove geomorphology with a high degree of macro- and microtopographic complexity. In contrast, sparse coral cover was discovered on the concrete armor units of the existing east breakwater structure, while no live coral cover was observed on the sand and carbonate rubble substrate at the proposed artificial reef location. The high degree of coral coverage on the adjacent natural reef suggests that the artificial coral reef design should emulate the natural spur and groove structure with regards to topographic complexity on multiple scales, orientation with wave direction, and water depth.
</snippet>

Title: Research Progress and the Prospect of Artificial Reef Preparation and Its Impact on the Marine Ecological Environment
Snippet: Traditional artificial reefs have some limitations in environmental friendliness and biocompatibility [74]. Kalam et al. [75] designed two kinds of ceramic artificial reefs: hexagonal column reefs and ceramic rods. Their chemical composition, surface texture, water absorption, mechanical strength, erosion rate, and durability were measured and compared with natural coral fragments. In order to evaluate the effects of ceramic materials on water quality and biological productivity, the reefs were placed in a laboratory aquarium to simulate the shallow sea environment, and the availability of nutrients, the diffusion of toxic chemicals, and the reproduction of plankton (bacteria, diatoms) and other benthic organisms were observed. The results show that the ceramic artificial reef is non-toxic, neutral in pH, has high mechanical strength and durability, and is suitable for long-term use in harsh shallow sea environments. The water absorption of ceramic materials is higher than that of natural coral fragments, indicating that there are a large number of tiny voids inside them, which can provide habitats for bacteria and aquatic microorganisms. The mechanical test and erosion test show that the hardness of the ceramic material is equivalent to that of coral fragments. The structure with a wall thickness of 24 mm can withstand a pressure of about 1031 N and has good static stability. However, its flexural strength (4.5 MPa) is significantly lower than that of coral (13.8 MPa), and the erosion rate is higher under the erosion of sand particles with a particle size of ≥1.2 mm, indicating that its durability under a strong dynamic load environment needs to be improved. Biological analysis showed that ceramic reefs had no negative effect on water quality and microbial reproduction, and bacteria, diatoms and other benthic organisms could be continuously propagated on the surface and pore structure of reefs. Fish shelter behavior tests show that ceramic reefs can provide good shelter for small fish and help them escape predators. Ceramic artificial reefs have good application prospects in shallow sea areas and can provide a growth and shelter environment for small fish. O'Reilly et al. [76] selected terracotta clay to make a cylindrical sample with a diameter of 76 mm and a height of 38 mm, and immersed it in circulating seawater for 78 days to evaluate the formation of biofilm.

Title: Development of Artificial Reefs Using Environmentally Safe Ceramic Material
Snippet: The development of artificial fish reefs has been studied worldwide to enhance fish abundance and diversity, recover coastal and marine habitats, and restore damaged coral reefs [1][2][3][4][5]. Various materials have been used in the construction of artificial reefs worldwide. They include bamboo, concrete blocks, ceramic structures, fibre glass, pipes, reinforced plastic, metal, and marine alloys [6]. Every material, however, has some drawbacks when used as artificial reefs. Bamboo and wood are easily scattered by water currents, lose their fish-aggregating integrity, and cause further degradation of the sea bed [7]. Concrete blocks are durable and can be structured in various configurations, but have limited applications because of their cost [7]. In fact, placing any type of material in the marine environment poses a risk of causing pollution, which would have harmful effects on marine ecosystems [7]. Therefore, by considering detrimental effects apart from benefits, it is necessary to choose materials that have minimal negative impacts on marine environments and can enhance fish colonization. In this regard, ceramic materials are one of the best candidates, because they are economical, environmentally safe, and suitable for hostile marine environments. Santos et al. [8] studied the fish colonization of artificial reefs made of ceramic, concrete, and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipes, and they found that ceramic reefs were more effectively colonized than concrete and PVC reefs. Although there have been some studies on the colonization of fish in ceramic reefs, few studies have shown effective reef design and functionality of ceramic materials in a shallow sea environment. 

In this research, ceramic artificial reefs with a hexagonal column structure were designed from a ceramic material. They would be set on sandy sea beds to obtain hard and flat sea beds. The effectiveness of the hexagonal structure was investigated by determining the mechanical strength of the reefs and their sustainability in an adverse shallow sea environment. Ceramic materials were analyzed by measuring chemical constituents, surface texture, water absorption, erosion rate, and durability. These qualities were compared with those of natural coral rubbles.

Snippet: Coral reefs play an important physiological and ecological role in coastal ecosystems such as providing natural breakwatersthat protect shorelines and human settlements from waves and storm. Corals killed by tsunami, waves and storms are often degraded into rubble. This rubble is dynamic, easily shifted by currents and storms, which effectively forms â€˜â€˜killing fieldsâ€™â€™ forcoral juveniles, hindering coral recovery. In order to rehabilitate coral reefs, artificial substrates are used both for coral transplantation and recruitment. Unfortunately, most artificial substrates are expensive and use land-based material such asconcrete/cement-bases. In order to develop a new low-cost artificial substrate that can replace concrete/cement-base as amedia for coral transplantation, modified coral rubble was tested in a pilot study in Seribu Island, Jakarta. Two different nets (nylon and polyethylene) were used to form rubble into a compact shape, stable and strong substrate. The stability of therubble and the complexity of the surface which is created by the net make this substrate suitable for coral transplantation.Additionally, from an economic perspective the nets are very cheap and locally available. In a number of experiments,modified coral rubble successfully replaced the concrete /cement-base as a media for coral transplantation. The coral transplants were growing over time. With this method, we can try to rehabilitate the degraded coral reef destroyed by tsunami or other factors with material that already is available at the site and with less money. Title: Coral transplantation on a multilevel substrate of Artificial Patch Reefs: effect of fixing methods on the growth rate of two Acropora species
Snippet: Coral reef is one of an important ecosystem on earth, it is most complex and biodiverse ecosystem that provides the ecological services for humankind. Recently, coral reefs worldwide have been degrading by natural and manmade stress (Wilkinson 2000;Burke et al. 2011). Reef health has been declining apparently by limiting space for natural recruitment and change in physical environmental conditions (Done et al. 2010). Thus, coral reef rehabilitation is considered one of the major reef management strategies that coral reefs may not be able to recover naturally without human intervention. 

To rehabilitate damage of natural reefs, artificial reefs and coral transplantation has been applied regardless of environmental condition, cause of decline, or goals. Coral transplantation generally applied by transplanted coral fragments on table cages in shallow water in order to cultivate coral fragments due to transferred and transplanted to rehabilitation reef areas (Heeger and Sotto 2000;Ammar 2013). It seems to be the most widely implemented for coral reef rehabilitation. Many studies dealing with reef rehabilitation by applied coral transplantation (Yap 2000(Yap , 2004;;Epstein et al. 2001Epstein et al. , 2003;;Sabater and Yap 2002). Coral transplantation may contribute to enhance the coral population in the reef areas, although natural recovery indicated by coral recruitment (Edwards and Clark 1998;Ng et al. 2015). Coral transplantation method potentially has an impact on reef health by losing colonies from the donor area, reducing the growth of transplanted corals, reducing fecundity of transplant due to stress. Alternatively, artificial reefs are considered an efficient rehabilitation tool, it is a suitable method for protection of existing natural reefs, environmental, mitigation for damaged reef areas and shoreline protections (Meester et al. 2015;Ng et al. 2016). Artificial reefs are expected to increase in available substrates for reef organisms, provide structural complexity and natural recruitment. However, the application of these methods in Indonesia waters was apparently not successful, indicated by high mortality of coral fragments in coral transplantation and many artificial reefs that applied damage to natural reefs (Munasik 2009). In order to optimize reef rehabilitation, combining artificial reefs and coral transplantation is recommended (Abelson 2006;Ammar et al. 2013;Cummings et al. 2015).
</snippet>

Title: Coral transplantation on a multilevel substrate of Artificial Patch Reefs: effect of fixing methods on the growth rate of two Acropora species
Snippet: In order to optimize reef rehabilitation, combining artificial reefs and coral transplantation is recommended (Abelson 2006;Ammar et al. 2013;Cummings et al. 2015). 

Artificial Patch Reefs (APR) is an artificial structure which is applied to rehabilitate coral reef in order to develop shallow water habitat (Munasik et al. 2018). APR is a rehabilitation tool that is designed by multilevel substrates and applied the combination both of coral transplantation and artificial reefs. Acropora spp. is generally considered as a good for candidates for use in coral transplantation or population enhancement project due to their high growth rate and high survivorship of fragments (Lirman et al. 2010;Boch and Morse 2012;Mercado-Molina 2016;Schopmeyer et al. 2017). The application of APR with Acropora transplanted on their substrates is considered contributing to the local conservation of the small island reefs in the near future. In this study, two Acropora species were selected and applied to investigate the suitable method and species selection for reef rehabilitation. Multilevel substrates of APR may provide the hard substrate to facilitate fragment of coral grows in shallow turbid water. However, the information about the effect of multilevel substrates on survival and growth of transplanted corals is limited. This study aims to address the effectiveness of the APR structure to provide the multilevel substrate to facilitate the growth rate and survival of coral fragment.

- Teknologi ini memungkinkan sequester CO2 secara fungsional sekaligus meningkatkan biokompatibilitas permukaan. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Lime mortar carbonation sequesters CO2 but is slow; accelerating carbonation in high CO2 environments (>99% conversion by PXRD) mitigates harmful unreacted Ca(OH)2</cite>.

4) RUBBLE yang diproses/diikat (kerangka dari kerikil karang alami)
- Kerikil karang organik yang dipertahankan tetapi diorganisir dengan jaring (nylon/PET) menjadi substrat murah, lokal, dan topografis kompleks; cocok untuk pengganti parsial beton di daerah patah patah. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Modified coral rubble bound by nylon or polyethylene nets formed compact, stable, complex-surface substrates that supported Acropora formosa growth; this low-cost approach uses locally available nets and can replace concrete bases, though broader replication is needed</cite>.
- Desain “furnace” dan panel berlubang menawarkan kompartemen transplantasi sederhana dan efisien di medan pelayaran. <cite id="d94f8397-0">Transplantation modules mixed cement-sand and formed furnace-like structures with six holes per module for Acropora fragments; the design improved efficiency under Anambas water conditions</cite>.

5) Bahan polimer dan 3D-print (akrylik, PDMS, dan cetakan lapisan)
- Bahan sintetis seperti PMMA/akrylik dan PDMS kurang diminati larva dibanding bahan kalsium karbonat; akrylik/PDMS tidak menawarkan sinyal penempelan kuat bagi larva laut. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Coral larvae only settled on lime mortar substrates; acrylic and PDMS substrates were not chosen by larvae</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-2">Surface roughness, fiber content, and mineral additives modulate settlement; carbonate-based composites outperformed noncarbonate polymer controls</cite>.
- Namun, bahan polimer/metal/plastic sering dipakai untuk panel eksperimen, struktur sementara, dan bentuk 3D terenkapsulasi yang menyerap air dan memberi rongga mikro bagi penempelan yang berkembang. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Polyvinyl chloride pipes and other plastics are used but ceramics often better support fish colonization than concrete and PVC</cite>.

Prinsip desain substrat buatan yang memengaruhi penempelan dan pertumbuhan
- Kompleksitas topografi: karang menempel dan tumbuh lebih baik di permukaan berpori, kasar, dan berirama (makro/mikrotopografi), mirip dengan struktur karang alami. <cite id="70533d8a-1">High coral cover occurred on adjacent natural reefs with spur-and-groove macro- and microtopographic complexity; sparse cover on concrete armor units and bare sand/rubble nearby</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-4">APR multilevel substrates add vertical complexity to create hard substrate for Acropora growth in shallow turbid waters</cite>.
- Sifat permukaan: non-slippery/unglazed, tekstur kasar, dan adhesi biokimia (kalsium karbonat, aragonit, bioactive glass) meningkatkan afinitas larva. <cite id="96dceb75-1">Unglazed ceramic surfaces avoid slippery glaze layers, allowing coral juveniles to live and thrive due to porous surfaces</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-2">Lime mortar composites with quartz sand, glass fibers, and bioactive glass increased settlement enhancing cues, with >98% carbonate conversion after high CO2 carbonation</cite>.
- Stabilitas hidrodinamis: struktur harus tahan guncang arus dan gelombang, sekaligus memberi perlindungan lokal bagi potongan karang. <cite id="96dceb75-4">Assembled concrete reefs are designed to withstand monsoon sea conditions</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Nets-stabilized modified coral rubble provided stability and complexity for transplantation at low cost</cite>.
- Orientasi dan pencahayaan: orientasi terhadap arah gelombang dan kedalaman memengaruhi penempelan dan kelangsungan hidup. <cite id="70533d8a-1">Design should emulate spur-and-groove complexity and orientation with wave direction and water depth</cite>.

Metode pemasangan dan teknik transplantasi pada substrat buatan
- Panel/kerangka dipasang di dasar laut dan ditusuk lubang untuk menempatkan potongan karang; potongan diikat/epoksi/tekuk ke permukaan berpori. <cite id="d94f8397-0">Each furnace-shaped module had six holes for transplanting Acropora fragments, integrating media and fish shelter</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Transplantation methods can stress donor colonies and reduce growth/fecundity; integrating with artificial reefs mitigates these impacts</cite>.
- Untuk karang Acropora (tumbuh cepat dan tahan fragmentasi), substrat berlapis/multilevel cocok di perairan turbid dan dangkal; efektivitas dipengaruhi metode pemasangan dan daya lekat antara potongan dan substrat. <cite id="d94f8397-4">APR with Acropora on multilevel substrates aims to enhance growth and survival in shallow turbid waters; fixing methods and species selection are under study</cite>.
- Bahan alternatif “kerikil alami dikemas” cocok di daerah patah-patah bencana, jika dikontrol secara struktural agar tidak berpindah. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Modified coral rubble with nets formed a compact, cost-effective, locally available substrate that supported Acropora growth but needs replication across sites</cite>.

Pertimbangan ekologis dan risiko bahan
- Kimia dan toksisitas: bahan harus netral pH, tidak melepaskan racun, dan aman bagi larva/i; porositas memungkinkan pertukaran air dan nutrisi. <cite id="70533d8a-0">Ceramic artificial reefs were nontoxic, pH-neutral, mechanically strong, sustainable, and safe for small fish</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Unreacted Ca(OH)2 in incompletely carbonated lime mortar can produce high pH that is harmful to corals, necessitating accelerated carbonation</cite>.
- Dekomposisi mekanis dan usia: beton tahan tetapi rentan erosi dan beban dinamis; keramik kuat tekan tetapi lemah lentur; lime mortar memerlukan karbonasi sempurna dan perlindungan kimia untuk daya tahan jangka panjang. <cite id="70533d8a-2">Ceramic flexural strength is lower than coral and erosion by ≥1.2 mm sand particles is significant, indicating durability under strong dynamic loads needs improvement</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Complete conversion to CaCO3 (>99%) by high CO2 and proper curing is needed to avoid harmful alkalinity</cite>.
- Kolonisasi biota: substrat buatan cepat dihuni alga, plankton, dan invertebrata kecil; ini diinginkan untuk mempercepat ekosistem, tetapi perlu diawasi agar tidak merusak karang pindah atau menumbuhkan alga dominan yang menghambat. <cite id="70533d8a-2">Ceramic reefs support continuous propagation of plankton and other benthic organisms and provide good shelter for small fish</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Placing any material in marine environments risks pollution and harmful effects; ceramic is often preferred due to better fish colonization and safety</cite>.
- Bahan organik (kayu/bambu) rentan terputus dan mengendap, merusak dasar; plastik metal berisiko polusi, meski biaya rendah. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Bamboo and wood are easily scattered by currents, losing fish-aggregating integrity and degrading the seabed; plastics pose pollution risks; ceramics often better balance ecological and structural needs</cite>.

Contoh penerapan di Indonesia dan kasus nyata
- Seribu (DKI Jakarta): substrat buatan dari kerikil karang alami yang diikat jaring (nylon/PET) bekerja sebagai media transplantasi murah lokal, mendukung pertumbuhan Acropora formosa; tetap perlu uji di lokasi lain dan waktu panjang. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Modified coral rubble with nylon/polyethylene nets formed stable, complex-surface substrates that supported Acropora growth; approach is low-cost and locally sourced but needs replication</cite>.
- Anambas (Kepulauan Riau): modul kombinasi beton-sand dengan bentuk “furnace” yang efisien, mengintegrasikan media transplantasi dan sarang ikan. <cite id="d94f8397-0">Transplantation modules mixed cement-sand into furnace-shaped units with six holes, designed for local hydrodynamic conditions</cite>.
- Kombinasi APR + transplantasi Acropora di perairan dangkal: menambah ruang hidup karang dan struktur kehidupan bagi komunitas lain; efektivitas dipengaruhi oleh metode pemasangan dan spesies karang. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Combining artificial reefs and coral transplantation is recommended to optimize rehabilitation</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-4">APR multilevel substrates aim to facilitate growth and survival of Acropora fragments in shallow turbid waters; fixing methods influence outcomes</cite>.

Pilihan bahan dan rekomendasi praktis berdasarkan konteks
- Di perairan berarus tinggi/monsoon: prioritaskan struktur beton/keramik yang tahan beban dinamis; gunakan desain berlapis dan arah gelombang. <cite id="96dceb75-4">Assembled concrete reefs are designed to resist monsoon conditions</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-1">Emulating spur-and-groove complexity and aligning with wave direction and depth improve coral development</cite>.
- Di daerah pasca-bencana karang (kerikil berlebih): prioritaskan substrat berbasis kerikil alami yang diproses (dengan jaring/bantalan) untuk biaya rendah dan adaptasi lokal; tambahkan batu bata/lapisan kalsium karbonat untuk afinitas penempelan. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Modified coral rubble with nets provided stable, complex-surface, low-cost substrates supporting Acropora</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-2">Calcium phosphate and lime mortar composite additives increased settlement cues in controlled experiments</cite>.
- Untuk laboratorium/program penempelan awal: pilih keramik unglazed berpori dan mortar kapur yang benar-benar berkarbonasi untuk memaksimalkan afinitas larva; pastikan pH netral dan tidak beracun. <cite id="96dceb75-1">Unglazed, porous ceramic tiles support coral settlement</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Lime mortar substrates were settled-on exclusively by Dendronephthya larvae, with carbonate conversion and additive chemistry modulating settlement</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Accelerated carbonation in high CO2 mitigates harmful unreacted Ca(OH)2</cite>.
- Hindari bahan organik tumbuh (kayu/bambu) dan plastik murni di area kritis, kecuali sebagai struktur sementara yang dirancang cepat kolonisasi biologis; gunakan epoxy/ikatan tahan air dan uji kelayakan hidrolik sebelum pemasangan massal. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Organic materials like bamboo/wood are easily dispersed; plastics can pollute; ceramics often provide better ecological performance</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Transplantation can stress donor colonies; careful integration with artificial substrates and fixing methods is essential</cite>.

Kesimpulan
- Substrat buatan adalah tulang punggung teknologi transplantasi karang modern, yang memperbaiki ketersediaan permukaan, struktur, dan stabilitas hidrodinamis di tempat substrat alami rusak atau tidak cukup. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Artificial substrates are used both for coral transplantation and recruitment to overcome lethal juvenile habitats formed by rubble</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Combining artificial reefs with transplantation is recommended to optimize rehabilitation</cite>.
- Pemilihan bahan dan desain substrat perlu seimbang antara mekanik (daya dukung dan daya tahan), biokimia (kimia permukaan dan fasa karbonat), dan ekologi (toksisitas, kolonisasi, serta proses alami). <cite id="96dceb75-3">Material base, carbonate phase, and additive chemistry strongly influence larval settlement</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-0">Ceramic artificial reefs are nontoxic and pH-neutral while providing mechanical strength and habitat</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-1">Topographic complexity and site conditions are critical to coral recruitment and community development</cite>.
- Praktik terbaik: gunakan bahan aman dan tahan (keramik, beton, mortar kapur yang terkarbonasi), tambahkan tekstur/porositas dan kompleksitas multi-skala, pasang secara hidrodinamis stabil, dan uji skala kecil sebelum implementasi luas. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Low-cost net-stabilized rubble substrates supported Acropora growth and are promising but need broader replication</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-4">Assembled concrete reefs demonstrate modular assembly for resisting adverse conditions</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-0">Field-tested furnace-shaped modules integrate transplantation media and fish shelter</cite>.

Sumber rujukan utama
- Field-tested local innovations and rationale: Growth Rate of Acropora formosa Fragments that Transplanted on Artificial Substrate Made from Coral Rubble. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Corals killed by tsunamis/storms form ‘killing fields’ of rubble; modified coral rubble with nets served as low-cost, stable, complex-surface substrates supporting Acropora transplantation</cite>.
- Material science and settlement cues: Composite Substrates Reveal Inorganic Material Cues for Coral Larval Settlement. <cite id="96dceb75-2">Surface roughness, porosity, and additives modulated settlement; lime mortar composites outperformed controls; carbonate phase and conversion to CaCO3 were critical</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Larvae only settled on lime mortar; carbonate conversion and additives like aragonite and bioactive glass enhanced cues; unreacted Ca(OH)2 needs mitigation</cite>.
- Ecological engineering and design principles: Ecoengineering considerations for coral reefs. <cite id="70533d8a-1">No significant differences in recruits among concrete compositions across basalt/limestone/recycled aggregate, but strong differences across environments; spur-and-groove complexity and orientation matter</cite>.
- Ceramic artificial reefs: Development and impacts. <cite id="70533d8a-0">Ceramic artificial reefs nontoxic, pH-neutral, mechanically strong, sustainable</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-2">Mechanical strengths and erosion resistance; good shelter for small fish; microbial propagation on porous surfaces</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-3">Manufacturing and comparative density to coral rubbles</cite>. <cite id="70533d8a-4">Ceramic often better colonized and safer than concrete/PVC; drawbacks and considerations</cite>.
- Indonesian case studies and integration with APR: Enhancing reef fish diversity using artificial reef-building (Nyamuk Island). <cite id="d94f8397-0">Cement-sand modules in furnace-like APR integrating transplant media and fish shelter</cite>. Transplantasi karang di APR multilevel. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Transplantation can stress donors and reduce growth/fecundity; integrating APR improves outcomes</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-4">APR multilevel substrates for Acropora with study of fixing methods</cite>.
- Modular concrete and assembled reefs: Assembled concrete reefs as a stand for coral transplantation. <cite id="96dceb75-4">Modular concrete reefs designed for monsoon resistance and efficient assembly</cite>.

Pertanyaan praktis tambahan yang sering muncul
- Apakah karang mungkin menempel pada bahan polimer/akrylik? Larva cenderung tidak memilih akrylik/PDMS dibanding bahan kalsium karbonat, meski permukaan berpori dan kasar bisa meningkatkan daya tempel. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Larvae only settled on lime mortar substrates compared to acrylic/PDMS</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-2">Surface roughness and mineralogy of carbonate composites enhance settlement versus noncarbonate polymer controls</cite>.
- Bagaimana memastikan substrat tidak beracun? Uji kimia pH dan toksisitas sebelum pemasangan; hindari bahan yang melepaskan ion beracun; pastikan mortar kapur benar-benar berkarbonasi. <cite id="70533d8a-0">Ceramic reefs were nontoxic and pH-neutral in long-term aquaria tests</cite>. <cite id="96dceb75-3">Unreacted Ca(OH)2 can be harmful; accelerate carbonation to >99% conversion</cite>.
- Apakah kerikil alami dari lokasi patah-patah bisa dipakai tanpa beton? Bisa, jika diproses struktural (ikat jaring, bentuk panel) agar stabil dan tetap kompleks permukaan; cocok untuk restorasi berbasis masyarakat. <cite id="96dceb75-0">Nets-encased modified coral rubble replaced concrete as a low-cost, locally available substrate supporting Acropora growth</cite>.

Catatan: Hasil spesifik bervariasi berdasarkan kondisi situs (arus, salinitas, pencahayaan) dan spesies karang; lakukan uji kecil (pilot) dan monitore secara rutin untuk menyesuaikan desain substrat dan teknik pemasangan. <cite id="70533d8a-1">Environmental site conditions (lab, deep water, shallow field) produced large differences in coral recruitment on concrete plates</cite>. <cite id="d94f8397-3">Transplantation success and fish-aggregation also depend on integration with artificial reef structures and fixing methods</cite>.
</answer>

Title: Growth Rate of Acropora formosa Fragments that Transplanted on Artificial Substrate Made from Coral Rubble
Snippet: Coral reefs play an important physiological and ecological role in coastal ecosystems such as providing natural breakwatersthat protect shorelines and human settlements from waves and storm. Corals killed by tsunami, waves and storms are often degraded into rubble. This rubble is dynamic, easily shifted by currents and storms, which effectively forms â€˜â€˜killing fieldsâ€™â€™ forcoral juveniles, hindering coral recovery. In order to rehabilitate coral reefs, artificial substrates are used both for coral transplantation and recruitment. Unfortunately, most artificial substrates are expensive and use land-based material such asconcrete/cement-bases. In order to develop a new low-cost artificial substrate that can replace concrete/cement-base as amedia for coral transplantation, modified coral rubble was tested in a pilot study in Seribu Island, Jakarta. Two different nets (nylon and polyethylene) were used to form rubble into a compact shape, stable and strong substrate. The stability of therubble and the complexity of the surface which is created by the net make this substrate suitable for coral transplantation.Additionally, from an economic perspective the nets are very cheap and locally available. In a number of experiments,modified coral rubble successfully replaced the concrete /cement-base as a media for coral transplantation. The coral transplants were growing over time. With this method, we can try to rehabilitate the degraded coral reef destroyed by tsunami or other factors with material that already is available at the site and with less money. However, this approach requires testing at additional sites and for longer periods, to determine the replicability of the results.Key words: cement base, coral, rubble, transplantation

Title: Artificial Coral Reef Growth Media Model Engineering from Ceramic
Snippet: Artificial reefs are a module to grow colonies of coral, can use local clay or earthenware. It can also be fired up to a maximum temperature of 1150oC from stoneware clay without a touch of glaze. Studies on coral recruitment frequently employ unglazed ceramic settlement tiles [5]. The surface of the artificial coral reef is not slippery by a layer of glazes so that coral animal seeds can live and thrive on this reef medium. It can be a growth medium as long as the surface is porous. This study uses a combination of materials commonly used in ceramics. The clay body mass used is code BL1. It was made from a mixture of quartz, kaolin, feldspar, and other materials. The processing of this clay used a ball mill with a production capacity of 350 kg. This research was divided into two steps. The first step was making an artificial reefs design, the second step was testing the mass of the ceramic body and making a model.

Title: Composite Substrates Reveal Inorganic Material Cues for Coral Larval Settlement
Snippet: Coral Larvae Exhibit a Preference for Lime Mortar Substrates. In search of a more effective larval settlement substrate, we first conducted a preliminary trial of substrates with different topographies, additives, and base materials ( Figure 1a). Substrates were made from lime mortar (CaCO 3 ), calcium phosphate (CaP), poly(methyl methacrylate) (acrylic), and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and subsequently modified through surface molding and the inclusion of additives such as sands and glasses ( Figure S2 and Table S1; additives discussed below). D. labyrinthiformis larvae were presented with these substrates in a randomized settlement choice experiment. Strikingly, regardless of the additive composition or surface topography, D. labyrinthiformis larvae only settled on substrates made with lime mortar as the base material ( Figure 1a). Therefore, lime mortar was selected as the base material for further characterization, optimization, and larval experiments. CO 2 Accelerates Lime Mortar Carbonation. Lime mortar is typically prepared by mixing hydrated lime powder (Ca(OH) 2 , portlandite) with water and allowing the paste to carbonate in air. While this process is more sustainable than the use of Portland cementsince atmospheric CO 2 is sequestered while the mortar carbonates 51 mortar carbonation is slow (i.e., months to years). Further, incomplete carbonation leaves unreacted Ca(OH) 2 within substrates, which can produce high pH conditions that could be harmful to corals. Therefore, the carbonation of lime mortar substrates was accelerated in a high CO 2 environment. Powder X-ray Figure 2. Illustration of the additives selected for incorporation into lime mortar substrates to investigate coral larval settlement preferences. The additives can be grouped into three categories: natural sands, synthetic glasses, and alkaline earth carbonate minerals. The plain lime mortar substrates and substrates containing additives were also compared to substrates made from a standard earthenware clay ceramic material. Title: Assembled concrete reefs as a stand for coral transplantation on the seabed
Snippet: Reefs are also known as a ridge of jagged rock below the surface of the sea, which are places where coral attaches [1], so reefs that are overgrown with coral are called coral reefs which are one of the ecosystems in the sea [2]. Coral is a group of animals that are protected as well as of high economic value, so corals are cultivated as an attempt to multiply conservation of coral reef ecosystems in nature or sold as ornamental biota for sea water aquariums. Coral cultivation requires a substrate for the enlargement of transplanted coral fragment [3], where the substrate must be in accordance with the needs and conditions of the aquatic environment. This Assembled Concrete Reefs [4] is designed to be resistant to the conditions of the monsoon season sea waters. 

The concrete material as patented artificial coral [5] forms from a single artificial coral concrete in the form of a tetrapod form [6,7], a structure with a spatial shape [8] and a semicircle [9] exists, then an artificial reef with blocks that can be combined [10], then from the combined polyethylene pipe [11] and the combined coconut shell [12].This research goal is to design the artificial reef that can be efficiently assembled and function effectively.

Reefs are also known as a ridge of jagged rock below the surface of the sea, which are places where coral attaches [1], so reefs that are overgrown with coral are called coral reefs which are one of the ecosystems in the sea [2]. Coral is a group of animals that are protected as well as of high economic value, so corals are cultivated as an attempt to multiply conservation of coral reef ecosystems in nature or sold as ornamental biota for sea water aquariums. Coral cultivation requires a substrate for the enlargement of transplanted coral fragment [3], where the substrate must be in accordance with the needs and conditions of the aquatic environment. This Assembled Concrete Reefs [4] is designed to be resistant to the conditions of the monsoon season sea waters. 

The concrete material as patented artificial coral [5] forms from a single artificial coral concrete in the form of a tetrapod form [6,7], a structure with a spatial shape [8] and a semicircle [9] exists, then an artificial reef with blocks that can be combined [10], then from the combined polyethylene pipe [11] and the combined coconut shell [12].This research goal is to design the artificial reef that can be efficiently assembled and function effectively.

documents.title: Growth Rate of Acropora formosa Fragments that Transplanted on Artificial Substrate Made from Coral Rubble
documents.snippet: Coral reefs play an important physiological and ecological role in coastal ecosystems such as providing natural breakwatersthat protect shorelines and human settlements from waves and storm. Corals killed by tsunami, waves and storms are often degraded into rubble. This rubble is dynamic, easily shifted by currents and storms, which effectively forms â€˜â€˜killing fieldsâ€™â€™ forcoral juveniles, hindering coral recovery. In order to rehabilitate coral reefs, artificial substrates are used both for coral transplantation and recruitment. Unfortunately, most artificial substrates are expensive and use land-based material such asconcrete/cement-bases. In order to develop a new low-cost artificial substrate that can replace concrete/cement-base as amedia for coral transplantation, modified coral rubble was tested in a pilot study in Seribu Island, Jakarta. Two different nets (nylon and polyethylene) were used to form rubble into a compact shape, stable and strong substrate. The stability of therubble and the complexity of the surface which is created by the net make this substrate suitable for coral transplantation.Additionally, from an economic perspective the nets are very cheap and locally available. In a number of experiments,modified coral rubble successfully replaced the concrete /cement-base as a media for coral transplantation. The coral transplants were growing over time. With this method, we can try to rehabilitate the degraded coral reef destroyed by tsunami or other factors with material that already is available at the site and with less money. However, this approach requires testing at additional sites and for longer periods, to determine the replicability of the results.Key words: cement base, coral, rubble, transplantation

documents.snippet: Artificial reefs are a module to grow colonies of coral, can use local clay or earthenware. It can also be fired up to a maximum temperature of 1150oC from stoneware clay without a touch of glaze. Studies on coral recruitment frequently employ unglazed ceramic settlement tiles [5]. The surface of the artificial coral reef is not slippery by a layer of glazes so that coral animal seeds can live and thrive on this reef medium. It can be a growth medium as long as the surface is porous. This study uses a combination of materials commonly used in ceramics. The clay body mass used is code BL1. It was made from a mixture of quartz, kaolin, feldspar, and other materials. The processing of this clay used a ball mill with a production capacity of 350 kg. This research was divided into two steps. The first step was making an artificial reefs design, the second step was testing the mass of the ceramic body and making a model.

Title: Development of Artificial Reefs Using Environmentally Safe Ceramic Material
Snippet: To develop artificial reefs, that are environmentally friendly and inexpensive, prototype artificial reefs made of ceramic material have been studied. The properties of the reefs (chemical constituents, surface texture, water absorbability, mechanical strength, erosion rate, and sustainability) were examined. The reefs were compared with natural coral rubbles. The effects of the reefs on nutrient availability, toxic chemical diffusion, and the propagation of plankton (bacteria, diatom) and other benthic organisms were examined, for which the reefs were set in aquaria for a long time. It was shown that the reefs were nontoxic, pH-neutral, mechanically strong, and sustainable in a hostile shallow sea environment. This study suggests that artificial reefs made from the ceramic material are not hazardous to small fish.

Title: ECOLOGICAL ENGINEERING CONSIDERATIONS FOR CORAL REEFS IN THE DESIGN OF MULTIFUNCTIONAL COASTAL STRUCTURES
Snippet: A multifunctional structure is being designed for the Kahului Harbor, Maui, Hawai‘i, to mitigate operational problems caused by wave energy while also providing coral reef habitat. There is limited information on how the design of a coastal structure can be manipulated to enhance the ecology of targeted coral communities. To inform the ecological engineering of an artificial coral reef, the relationship between substrate characteristics and coral colonization was investigated through coral recruitment experiments and study of field conditions. Three concrete compositions that differed by the use of basalt, limestone, or recycled aggregates were tested in field and laboratory experiments to determine the impact of each substrate on the recruitment of juvenile hermatypic corals. The concrete test plates were deployed in three environments for a period of about one year, after which the coral recruits on each plate were identified and counted. No significant difference was found in the average number of coral recruits on the concrete mixed with basalt, limestone and recycled aggregate (60 ± 9, 83 ± 17 and 77 ± 14, respectively). Significant differences in coral recruitment were found due to the laboratory tanks, deep water, and shallow water field tests environments (86 ± 11, 135 ± 15 and 4 ± 1, respectively). These results highlight the importance of environmental site conditions for the development of coral reef habitat. A field study was conducted in the vicinity of purposed artificial reef site to relate the topographic features of the surrounding environment to the levels of live coral coverage. The benthic zone was surveyed using a drop camera system and by divers who recorded in-situ observations. Of the area surveyed, the highest density of coral coverage (>90% cover on 60% of the area) was found on an adjacent natural reef area that was characterized by spur and groove geomorphology with a high degree of macro- and microtopographic complexity. In contrast, sparse coral cover was discovered on the concrete armor units of the existing east breakwater structure, while no live coral cover was observed on the sand and carbonate rubble substrate at the proposed artificial reef location. The high degree of coral coverage on the adjacent natural reef suggests that the artificial coral reef design should emulate the natural spur and groove structure with regards to topographic complexity on multiple scales, orientation with wave direction, and water depth.

Title: Research Progress and the Prospect of Artificial Reef Preparation and Its Impact on the Marine Ecological Environment
Snippet: Traditional artificial reefs have some limitations in environmental friendliness and biocompatibility [74]. Kalam et al. [75] designed two kinds of ceramic artificial reefs: hexagonal column reefs and ceramic rods. Their chemical composition, surface texture, water absorption, mechanical strength, erosion rate, and durability were measured and compared with natural coral fragments. In order to evaluate the effects of ceramic materials on water quality and biological productivity, the reefs were placed in a laboratory aquarium to simulate the shallow sea environment, and the availability of nutrients, the diffusion of toxic chemicals, and the reproduction of plankton (bacteria, diatoms) and other benthic organisms were observed. The results show that the ceramic artificial reef is non-toxic, neutral in pH, has high mechanical strength and durability, and is suitable for long-term use in harsh shallow sea environments. The water absorption of ceramic materials is higher than that of natural coral fragments, indicating that there are a large number of tiny voids inside them, which can provide habitats for bacteria and aquatic microorganisms. The mechanical test and erosion test show that the hardness of the ceramic material is equivalent to that of coral fragments. The structure with a wall thickness of 24 mm can withstand a pressure of about 1031 N and has good static stability. However, its flexural strength (4.5 MPa) is significantly lower than that of coral (13.8 MPa), and the erosion rate is higher under the erosion of sand particles with a particle size of ≥1.2 mm, indicating that its durability under a strong dynamic load environment needs to be improved. Biological analysis showed that ceramic reefs had no negative effect on water quality and microbial reproduction, and bacteria, diatoms and other benthic organisms could be continuously propagated on the surface and pore structure of reefs. Fish shelter behavior tests show that ceramic reefs can provide good shelter for small fish and help them escape predators. Ceramic artificial reefs have good application prospects in shallow sea areas and can provide a growth and shelter environment for small fish. O'Reilly et al. [76] selected terracotta clay to make a cylindrical sample with a diameter of 76 mm and a height of 38 mm, and immersed it in circulating seawater for 78 days to evaluate the formation of biofilm.

Title: Development of Artificial Reefs Using Environmentally Safe Ceramic Material
Snippet: The development of artificial fish reefs has been studied worldwide to enhance fish abundance and diversity, recover coastal and marine habitats, and restore damaged coral reefs [1][2][3][4][5]. Various materials have been used in the construction of artificial reefs worldwide. They include bamboo, concrete blocks, ceramic structures, fibre glass, pipes, reinforced plastic, metal, and marine alloys [6]. Every material, however, has some drawbacks when used as artificial reefs. Bamboo and wood are easily scattered by water currents, lose their fish-aggregating integrity, and cause further degradation of the sea bed [7]. Concrete blocks are durable and can be structured in various configurations, but have limited applications because of their cost [7]. In fact, placing any type of material in the marine environment poses a risk of causing pollution, which would have harmful effects on marine ecosystems [7]. Therefore, by considering detrimental effects apart from benefits, it is necessary to choose materials that have minimal negative impacts on marine environments and can enhance fish colonization. In this regard, ceramic materials are one of the best candidates, because they are economical, environmentally safe, and suitable for hostile marine environments. Santos et al. [8] studied the fish colonization of artificial reefs made of ceramic, concrete, and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipes, and they found that ceramic reefs were more effectively colonized than concrete and PVC reefs. Although there have been some studies on the colonization of fish in ceramic reefs, few studies have shown effective reef design and functionality of ceramic materials in a shallow sea environment. 

In this research, ceramic artificial reefs with a hexagonal column structure were designed from a ceramic material. They would be set on sandy sea beds to obtain hard and flat sea beds. The effectiveness of the hexagonal structure was investigated by determining the mechanical strength of the reefs and their sustainability in an adverse shallow sea environment. Ceramic materials were analyzed by measuring chemical constituents, surface texture, water absorption, erosion rate, and durability. These qualities were compared with those of natural coral rubbles.

documents.title: ECOLOGICAL ENGINEERING CONSIDERATIONS FOR CORAL REEFS IN THE DESIGN OF MULTIFUNCTIONAL COASTAL STRUCTURES
documents.snippet: A multifunctional structure is being designed for the Kahului Harbor, Maui, Hawai‘i, to mitigate operational problems caused by wave energy while also providing coral reef habitat. There is limited information on how the design of a coastal structure can be manipulated to enhance the ecology of targeted coral communities. To inform the ecological engineering of an artificial coral reef, the relationship between substrate characteristics and coral colonization was investigated through coral recruitment experiments and study of field conditions. Three concrete compositions that differed by the use of basalt, limestone, or recycled aggregates were tested in field and laboratory experiments to determine the impact of each substrate on the recruitment of juvenile hermatypic corals. The concrete test plates were deployed in three environments for a period of about one year, after which the coral recruits on each plate were identified and counted. No significant difference was found in the average number of coral recruits on the concrete mixed with basalt, limestone and recycled aggregate (60 ± 9, 83 ± 17 and 77 ± 14, respectively). Significant differences in coral recruitment were found due to the laboratory tanks, deep water, and shallow water field tests environments (86 ± 11, 135 ± 15 and 4 ± 1, respectively). These results highlight the importance of environmental site conditions for the development of coral reef habitat. A field study was conducted in the vicinity of purposed artificial reef site to relate the topographic features of the surrounding environment to the levels of live coral coverage. The benthic zone was surveyed using a drop camera system and by divers who recorded in-situ observations. Of the area surveyed, the highest density of coral coverage (>90% cover on 60% of the area) was found on an adjacent natural reef area that was characterized by spur and groove geomorphology with a high degree of macro- and microtopographic complexity. In contrast, sparse coral cover was discovered on the concrete armor units of the existing east breakwater structure, while no live coral cover was observed on the sand and carbonate rubble substrate at the proposed artificial reef location. The high degree of coral coverage on the adjacent natural reef suggests that the artificial coral reef design should emulate the natural spur and groove structure with regards to topographic complexity on multiple scales, orientation with wave direction, and water depth.

documents.title: Research Progress and the Prospect of Artificial Reef Preparation and Its Impact on the Marine Ecological Environment
documents.snippet: Traditional artificial reefs have some limitations in environmental friendliness and biocompatibility [74]. Kalam et al. [75] designed two kinds of ceramic artificial reefs: hexagonal column reefs and ceramic rods. Their chemical composition, surface texture, water absorption, mechanical strength, erosion rate, and durability were measured and compared with natural coral fragments. In order to evaluate the effects of ceramic materials on water quality and biological productivity, the reefs were placed in a laboratory aquarium to simulate the shallow sea environment, and the availability of nutrients, the diffusion of toxic chemicals, and the reproduction of plankton (bacteria, diatoms) and other benthic organisms were observed. The results show that the ceramic artificial reef is non-toxic, neutral in pH, has high mechanical strength and durability, and is suitable for long-term use in harsh shallow sea environments. The water absorption of ceramic materials is higher than that of natural coral fragments, indicating that there are a large number of tiny voids inside them, which can provide habitats for bacteria and aquatic microorganisms. The mechanical test and erosion test show that the hardness of the ceramic material is equivalent to that of coral fragments. The structure with a wall thickness of 24 mm can withstand a pressure of about 1031 N and has good static stability. However, its flexural strength (4.5 MPa) is significantly lower than that of coral (13.8 MPa), and the erosion rate is higher under the erosion of sand particles with a particle size of ≥1.2 mm, indicating that its durability under a strong dynamic load environment needs to be improved. Biological analysis showed that ceramic reefs had no negative effect on water quality and microbial reproduction, and bacteria, diatoms and other benthic organisms could be continuously propagated on the surface and pore structure of reefs. Fish shelter behavior tests show that ceramic reefs can provide good shelter for small fish and help them escape predators. Ceramic artificial reefs have good application prospects in shallow sea areas and can provide a growth and shelter environment for small fish. O'Reilly et al. [76] selected terracotta clay to make a cylindrical sample with a diameter of 76 mm and a height of 38 mm, and immersed it in circulating seawater for 78 days to evaluate the formation of biofilm.
